# Attachment Rules

A reusable Compute Definition extending Party Access Functions. It validates parent–instruction party compatibility, checks callers, and compiles attachment hooks into action bindings. Its functions perform checks or return configuration; calling them does not itself attach a document or complete an action.

## Party and caller checks

`checkRoster(parent, child, authority, cross)` requires a nonempty parent roster. Every parent role must exist in the child with matching primary details. The child may add only the role named by `authority`, which must exist in the child. When `cross` is true, that authority role must also exist in the parent.

`samePrimary(left, right)` requires both `lead/channel` values and compares their exact Blue identities. Both `readerKeys` lists must be nonempty, contain no duplicates, and have equal membership regardless of order. Missing lists are read as empty and therefore fail these checks. Representatives are not compared by this function.

`requireCaller()` requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be exactly true, otherwise rejecting with `ATTACHMENT_EXACT_REVIEW_REQUIRED`. It then calls `requireActive` with `call/channel` and `workflow: true`. If `/activation` exists, this requires an active document, valid participant access, and a channel matching a current party role or a representative channel named `role__repId`. Missing `active` is treated as false by this check. If `/activation` is absent, these inherited activation checks are skipped; the exact-version requirement remains.

`origin(document)` returns the exact Blue identity of that argument’s `/contracts/initialized/document`, rejecting if it is absent.

## Hook configuration

`compileHooks(allowed, hooks, key)` accepts action names in `allowed`, a `hooks` map organized by action and hook name, and an attachment `key`. Unknown actions are rejected. Hook names must be nonempty text containing none of `.`, `/`, `~`, or `__`.

Each hook uses:

- `in`: `instruction` by default, or `parent`.
- `on`: `workflow` by default. Instruction hooks require `workflow`; parent hooks require an explicit `state` or `event` mode.
- `event`: required for a parent event hook.
- `path` and `equals`: required for a parent state hook; `path` must begin with `/`. The action is gated by equality with the parent value at that path, together with `when`, whose omitted value is treated as true.
- `params`, `before`, and `after`: preserved in the compiled binding, subject to the recheck restrictions below. Parent safety checks are prepended to any supplied `before` steps.

The result contains `bindings`, `parentDependencies`, `signals`, and `relationship`. `relationship` is `cross-embedded` if any hook uses the parent, otherwise `one-way`. Each parent dependency records `action`, `hook`, `on`, and `path`; the recorded path defaults to an empty string when omitted.

Parent hooks become `embedded` bindings at `/sources/parent`. A parent state hook adds a signal descriptor with `id` equal to `action_hookName` and its original parent `path`. Its event filter matches `Source Changed` with `attachment: key` and `hook` equal to that signal ID. Compilation creates these descriptors and filters; it does not emit the signal.

## Parent guards and rechecks

Every compiled parent hook requires the parent’s selected instruction to have the same initialized-document identity as the executing instruction. Selection uses `/clauses/attachment/parameters/instructionPath` beneath `/sources/parent`, followed by `/contracts/initialized/document`, and compares it with the instruction’s own `/contracts/initialized/document`. A missing selected document makes this guard false.

Before the action, the parent must have `/sources/parent/activation/active` exactly true, contain the role named by `/clauses/attachment/parameters/authority`, and have primary channels and reader-key membership matching the instruction’s `/activation/parties` for every parent role. Failure rejects the action before user-supplied `before` steps.

`recheckOn` defaults to an empty list. Explicitly supplying it is allowed only for parent state hooks and forbids both `before` and `after`, even with an empty list. Each recheck path must begin with `/`, must not be `/` or start with `/sources`, and must be unique within that hook. These paths refer to the executing instruction’s own document.

Each path generates a local `change` binding named `hookName_recheck_0`, `hookName_recheck_1`, and so on. It retains the parent-state equality, selection guard, and safety checks, while removing the parent event filter. Collisions between authored and generated hook names are rejected.

For hooks explicitly declaring `recheckOn`, `checkStateExpression` examines `params` and `when`, using `{}` and true respectively when omitted. It rejects any nested object key named `$event`, `$binding`, `$var`, `$resultValue`, `$call`, `$const`, `$steps`, `$currentContract`, `$intrinsic`, `$events`, or `$changeset`. Traversal must finish within 32 passes; otherwise it rejects the expression as too deep.

## Inherited access and readiness

`readerGroups(readers, roster)` combines supplied reader groups with each party’s `readerKeys` and each representative’s `readerKeys`, using `role` and `role__repId` names. Roster-derived groups replace supplied groups with the same name. `transports(roster)` collects primary and representative channels under those names.

`accessValid(accessPaths, readers, roster)` skips access-document checks for External Channels. Other transports must be Timeline Channels. Each such transport needs at least one Timeline Access document at an `accessPaths` location that matches its timeline and provider and contains at least one allowed key from every reader group. All groups must be covered within that same matching access document; keys are not combined across documents for this check. Missing permission lists are treated as empty. An invalid access-document type rejects; an uncovered transport returns false. These checks inspect access state and do not grant access.

`businessReady()` returns true when `/activation` is absent. Otherwise it requires the document not to be closed, every role in `required` to have approval, `termsCurrent()` to succeed, and participant access to be valid. Here, missing `closed` and individual approvals default to false; missing `required`, `accessPaths`, `readers`, and `parties` use empty collections. `termsCurrent()` compares each saved value in `/activation/terms/fields` with its corresponding document path; a missing fields map means no comparisons. Unlike `requireActive`, `businessReady` does not check `active` or caller authority.

These helpers do not define the consuming actions’ effects or the mechanism that emits source signals. Passing their checks establishes neither a completed action nor the current reader’s permission to invoke one.
